Supabase's CDN ignores cache-control: re-uploading DIFFERENT bytes to the same object key returns the OLD content for up to an hour, and a deleted object stays readable. Verified (server-side size said 7 while download() returned the 3-byte original). Mitigated by content-addressed keys (<run_id>/<sha256[:12]>_<name>) so a key's bytes never change. NEVER build a bucket key by hand — use files.save_upload and the returned documents.storage_url.

No orphan cleanup in Storage: deleting a run removes its documents rows but leaves the objects. Content-addressing means every edited re-upload also leaves its predecessor. Fine at demo scale (1 GB free tier); sweep before deployment.

SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY must go into Streamlit Secrets at deploy time, never the repo. It bypasses all RLS and has full DB access. SUPABASE_KEY (anon) is currently unused — files.py uses service_role and the DB goes through SQLAlchemy, not PostgREST.

CUAD is inadequate as the primary contract source: 8 of 510 (1.6%) carry both a real recurring amount and a real escalation clause, and only 3 survive a hand read. ADR-013 demotes it to extraction-dev (Phase 5) and training volume (Phase 10). Do not build anomaly scenarios from CUAD alone.

NEVER put bare `escalat` in a keep-list. Measured on CUAD: 81 contracts match it, 68 mean the DISPUTE escalation procedure ('escalate to senior management'), not a price rise. The plan's KEEP list in implementation_plan.py contains it. Filter on a real percentage or CPI reference tied to a fee instead.

~24% of both CUAD and EDGAR redact financials with [***] under SEC confidential treatment. A contract can have a perfect escalation clause and still be unusable. Counter-intuitively the redacted pile is MORE varied (33 distinct clauses vs gold's 21, zero overlap) because boilerplate fee letters publish numbers while negotiated contracts hide them.

Counting documents overstates the corpus ~2.5x. EDGAR's 51 gold documents carry only 21 distinct escalation clauses — one administrator (Ultimus) sends every fund trust the same fee letter. Dedupe on clause fingerprint AND filer, never filename. Report DISTINCT CLAUSES, not document count. Near-duplicates either side of a train/test split are the invisible leak that makes Phase 11 meaningless.

Corpus variety is adequate (44) but not good: the EX-99 mutual-fund cluster is over-represented because edgar_probe.py used generic queries and read only PAGE 1 of each result list. Broader search designed but NOT RUN — industry-specific queries, pages 2-10, cap per filer. Do it before Phase 10, not Phase 3: variety is load-bearing only for training and the base-vs-tuned claim.

RESOLVED 2026-08-12 (found in Phase 4): core/storage/files.py's load()/delete() stripped `file://` naively (storage_url[len("file://"):]), which on Windows leaves a stray leading `/` before the drive letter (Path.as_uri() produces file:///C:/Users/... -- three slashes). WindowsPath then parses /C:/Users/... as a folder literally named `C:`, so is_file() was always False -- every local-backend load() call was silently broken. Phase 2's own 11 verification assertions only exercised the Supabase backend. Fixed with urllib.request.url2pathname + urlparse. Caught because Phase 4's CSV column-mapping step is the first code to call files.load() on a real local upload.

prompts.py has had exactly one iteration and STILL has not been tuned, but it has now been measured once (2026-08-14): PROMPT_VERSION v1 scored 10/10 valid and 80.0% grounding on 10 EDGAR contracts. The 3 dropped quotes were paraphrases -- the model was told 'character for character' and did not comply. That is the tuning work the plan budgets for, and it is still open; v1 is a measured baseline now, not a guess. Any edit here invalidates exactly its own cache entries (cache.key hashes the rendered prompt), so re-running the eval after a prompt change is cheap.

Grammar-constrained decoding is used when the server accepts response_format=json_schema (vLLM does; the transformers fallback does not), and llm_client negotiates downwards automatically. But NO valid-JSON-rate comparison has been run with it on versus off, so that row of the Phase 11 eval table is empty. The client-side repair-retry is kept regardless (ADR-004).

The .venv on THIS machine (Linux) is Python 3.14.6, not the 3.12.13 known issue #10 records. Streamlit Community Cloud does not offer 3.14, so the deployment-parity guarantee #10 was created to give does not currently hold here. Everything installs and runs on 3.14; the risk is a wheel or behaviour difference discovered at deploy time. Rebuild with `uv venv --python 3.12` before Phase 11, or pin runtime.txt and find out early.

Phase 5's grounding number PASSED EXACTLY ON THE LINE: 80.0%, being 12 grounded and 3 dropped of 15 quotes. One more paraphrase reads 73% and the phase fails. The sample is small enough to swing hard -- a 2-contract smoke run an hour earlier read 66.7%. Do not quote 80% as a stable capability of the model; it is one measurement at n=15. Re-run with --limit 20 before it is cited in the Phase 11 report.

'valid ContractRules 10/10' is softer than it reads. 3 of the 10 contracts (Mammoth Energy, Regal Entertainment, Vantiv) extracted ZERO clauses -- 0 grounded, 0 dropped -- and an empty ContractRules is structurally valid, so it scores as a pass while proving nothing. The yield is also lopsided: AMERI Holdings EX-99.1 alone produced 7 of the 12 grounded quotes. Report the split, not just the headline. The same shape showed on the CUAD PDF pass: 5 contracts yielded 2 locatable quotes, 3 yielded none. Consider adding a 'contracts with >=1 grounded clause' metric in Phase 11.

Two serving bugs that ONLY appear on real hardware, both fixed by notebook-cell workarounds recorded in README.md ('Starting a session'), neither fixed in code. (1) google.colab.userdata.get() reads secrets from the notebook KERNEL, so serve_model.py cannot see LLM_API_KEY when launched as `!python ...` -- it dies with "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'kernel'". Fix: read the secret in a cell, set os.environ, which serve_model.py already prefers. Kaggle's kaggle_secrets does NOT have this problem. (2) `pip install vllm` is unpinned and pulls a torch built for CUDA 13.0, leaving Colab's preinstalled torchaudio (CUDA 12.8) stale; transformers imports torchaudio unconditionally and the server never starts. Fix: pip uninstall torchaudio after installing vllm. Consider pinning vllm before deployment.

When vLLM's child process dies at import time, serve_model.py does not notice: it prints 'waiting for the model to finish loading (up to 900s)' and polls a dead port for the full 15 minutes before falling back. wait_until_ready() polls /v1/models but never checks Popen.poll(). One-line fix available; not made because the phase was being measured, not edited. Costs 15 minutes per failed start.

web/ (FastAPI + Jinja2, ADR-018) renders the delivered design but WRITES NOTHING. Every button is inert by design -- upload, 'Add to recoverable', 'Rule it out', 'Confirm and reconcile', the CSV mapping accept -- because the actions behind them are Phases 6-9. They keep the mockup's appearance rather than being greyed out, so do not read a fully-styled page as a working one. In live mode the agent panel and the Decision Engine verdict are deliberately empty (Phases 8 and 9), and no expense figures exist in any table, so no surplus can ever be computed from the current schema. UPDATED 2026-08-15: web/ now caches database reads for WEB_CACHE_SECONDS (default 15) in web/cache.py. That is only safe BECAUSE nothing writes -- the first write path added to web/ must call web.cache.clear() or the UI will show stale figures for up to 15 seconds after a user's own action.

A live web/ page cannot be made fast from this repo: the Supabase instance is in ap-southeast-1 and a single round trip measured 409 ms median (1127 ms for a fresh connection), so response time is query-count x 400 ms. Query count was cut 35 -> 9 (get_summary_stats 8 -> 3 round trips, get_client_totals 4 -> 1, plus a per-request memo), which took a cold page from 8.7 s to ~5 s; the read cache makes warm pages ~3 ms. The remaining ~5 s cold is network and needs a region change or a nearer pooler, not code. Demo mode renders in 4 ms and never touches the database. Do not 'optimise' the SQL -- it is not the SQL.

Escalation COMPOUNDS in core/engine/timeline_generator.py (6,000 -> 6,480 -> 6,998.40 on a 'each anniversary' clause) but data_sourcing/scenario_builder.py applies its escalation exactly ONCE. They agree today only because no scenario window contains a second anniversary -- every contract starts in 2024 and the observation year is 2025. A three-year scenario would diverge, and the ENGINE is the correct side (the clauses say 'on each anniversary'). Pass compound_escalation=False for a genuine one-off rise. Do not 'fix' the engine to match the scenario builder.

Milestones are NEVER billed automatically. ContractRules.Milestone carries a condition ('on website launch'), not a date, and nothing resolves one into the other -- generate_timeline leaves an undated milestone out and unresolved_milestones()/RunSummary.unresolved_milestones names it. Deliberate: guessing a due date manufactures ghost invoices. The pitch's own $15,000 launch milestone therefore needs milestones.due_date set by hand before it is ever checked. seed_demo.py sets one; a computed run does not.

web/ still writes NOTHING after Phase 6 (extends known issue #52). Reconciliation runs from the Streamlit app only -- app/components/reconcile_panel.py. web/'s 'Confirm and reconcile' button remains inert by design (ADR-018) and its tooltips now say where the action actually lives instead of naming a phase. THE FIRST WRITE PATH ADDED TO web/ MUST CALL web.cache.clear(); core.engine.pipeline.compute_run carries that warning in its docstring.

Reconciliation's date rule is ADR-019, not plain calendar-month grouping: a payment settles the most recent billing ON OR BEFORE its own date, within the same month or +/-15 days. One consequence to know before reading a demo: a client who pays two months at once with a single transfer reads as one month settled and one ghost_invoice. Phase 8's check_split_payments tool is where that gets caught -- the same trade ADR-006 already made.

NEVER score a fuzzy clause match with fuzz.partial_ratio alone. It normalises by its SHORTER argument, so a text block containing only the character '5' scores 100 against any quote containing a 5 -- Phase 7 shipped a confident amber box around exactly that digit on a table-of-contents page before this was caught. clause_locator now requires (a) the block to be at least half the quote's length, (b) a 35% overlap of distinctive words, and (c) _window_ratio: fuzz.ratio against a SAME-LENGTH slice. Regression-tested in tests/test_clause_locator.py.

Clause quotes are commonly wrapped in ellipses -- '...a monthly payment in addition to...' -- by a model and by a human transcriber alike, and the document contains no such dots. An exact PDF search for the quote as given therefore FAILS on a clause that is right there, and the fuzzy tier then picks something else. clause_locator strips leading/trailing ellipses and quotation marks before searching; that single change turned two wrong fuzzy boxes into exact hits on the Regal contract.

A located bbox is the UNION of every line the match spans, so on a multi-line clause the box includes whatever else shares those lines. Ordinary PDF-highlighting behaviour and honest, but it is not a word-perfect outline -- do not describe it as one in the report.

The clause page image costs ~4.9 s cold and 1.2 ms warm. The cost is documents.extracted_text -- a couple of hundred kilobytes for an EDGAR filing, pulled across the 400 ms ap-southeast-1 link (known issue #53) -- plus the render. Cached in web/cache.py and by the browser (Cache-Control private, max-age=600). Not fixable in code from this repo; a page-level text column or a nearer region would fix it.

Nothing re-locates clauses automatically. pipeline.locate_run_clauses runs from scripts/run_scenario.py and from the Reconcile button in app/. Editing a clause quote by hand, or re-extracting a contract, leaves STALE source_page/source_bbox until it is run again.

AMENDS #57 (not resolved by it). check_split_payments only finds combinations of SEVERAL transactions that SUM TO one target -- it cannot recognise a single transfer that is a MULTIPLE of one billing's amount (the actual shape of #57's two-months-in-one-transfer case). #57's own wording ('Phase 8's check_split_payments tool is where that gets caught') is optimistic and should not be quoted as solved. Closing it for real needs a tool that compares a client's actual total against several neighbouring months at once, which does not exist yet.

The plan's own Phase 8 worked example -- the agent flipping a name-variant false positive ('StarterLabs' vs 'Starter Labs') on the realistic scenario -- no longer reproduces. core.engine.reconciliation.attribute_transactions (Phase 6, built after the Phase 8 narrative was written) already fuzzy-matches client names at reconcile time, so every name variant in the shipped scenario is attributed correctly before the agent ever runs. Found by tracing the code and ground_truth.json BEFORE writing Phase 8, not by a failing demo. ADR-022 records the decision: prove the agent two other ways (scripts/eval_agent.py) instead of editing scenario_builder.py, which Phase 6 already measured and cited by exact figures in three places.

scripts/eval_agent.py -- the live-model half of Phase 8's proof -- has NOT been run against a live GPU. No Colab/Kaggle tunnel was available this session (same situation #40 first recorded in Phase 5). The graph's control-flow correctness (hard cap, persistence, never-lose-an-anomaly) is proven offline by tests/test_verification_agent.py regardless; whether the real 3B model reasons well enough to flip the synthetic fixture to false_positive is unmeasured. Re-run before citing agent quality in the final report.
